analysis.title: FOMC Pre / Macro Assets & Hiking Cycles / Luxury / GTT (up) / Reckitt / Saint Gobain / BNP / Novartis / Talanx / Europe Biotech
key_insights: GS US economics expects the FOMC to skip a hike at its October meeting and likely deliver a second hike in December, based on FOMC participants' comments pointing to a compromise of raising the funds rate every other meeting.

Market pricing of the Fed path has removed one hike and now peaks at just over 4.5%. GS baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are considerably less hawkish, because GS is skeptical the FOMC will hike four times and expects cuts later.
GS baseline of a modest number of hikes, growth around potential and gradual inflation relief points to a modestly positive path for equities.

History shows three risk scenarios for equities in a hiking cycle: an earlier end to tightening on better inflation news (most positive for risk assets), an interruption driven by growth or financial stress (at least initially less friendly), or a more extended cycle with resilient growth (raises the risk of a larger growth downgrade later).
Luxury 3Q26 wrap: China macro hit hard as expected, but the exit rate was better than July-August. GS thinks this bodes well for the Holiday season.

GS upgrades GTT (GTT.PA) to Buy from Neutral with a EUR210 12-month price target, implying about 16% upside, after a c.12% post-results share price correction. GTT is the global leader in LNG containment systems with an asset-light licensing model and near-100% share at major Asian shipyards.
Reckitt Q3 organic sales growth was +3.3% vs consensus +4.1%. Reported sales were in line. The miss came from the US, where Lysol (c.35% of US sales) had unexpected manufacturing constraints.
Reckitt (Buy) trades on 14.5x CY27E P/E, a 19% discount to the GS Staples sector vs parity historically. GS sees a buying opportunity after the Lysol one-off.

Saint-Gobain (Neutral) 3Q26 organic growth was +2.5%, vs VA consensus +2.7% and GSe +3.0%, slowing from +3.5% in 2Q as volumes weakened, particularly in France. Scandinavia and APAC were better. FY26 EBITDA margin guidance was maintained at >15%.

BNP Paribas Q3'26 results were strong despite a weaker Arval, with a new share buyback announced and a path to additional excess capital return at year-end. Revenues were c.3% above expectations, led by CIB (Equities c.30% above, FICC 2% below). Retail Banking missed by 2% on Arval (c.24% miss). Opex was in line and PPP was 4% above.

Novartis (Sell) had a strong 3Q26 profit beat driven by cost control. 12-month target prices are unchanged at CHF113 / ADR $136. GS says the stock trades near all-time highs at a c.7% premium to the sector on 2027E P/E despite significant patent expiration risk.
The note also lists a Talanx 3Q'26 earnings preview and a Europe biotech 3Q26 preview for commercial SMID caps, with no detail in the text provided.

market_movers.rationale: GTT upgraded to Buy from Neutral after a c.12% post-results correction. GS cites strong medium-term revenue visibility and a highly profitable asset-light licensing model.
Reckitt Q3 organic growth missed on Lysol manufacturing constraints in the US. GS sees a buying opportunity at 14.5x CY27E P/E, a 19% discount to the Staples sector.
Saint-Gobain 3Q26 organic growth of +2.5% slowed from +3.5% on weaker volumes, with FY26 EBITDA margin guidance kept at >15%.
Novartis beat on profit through cost control, but GS sees a c.7% premium to the sector on 2027E P/E and patent expiration risk not adequately priced.

BNP Paribas Q3'26 (reported): revenues c.3% above expectations, Equities c.30% above, FICC 2% below, Retail Banking 2% miss, Arval c.24% miss, PPP 4% above, opex in line. A new share buyback was announced.
